resource: One PostgreSQL backend message on the first-slice production root profile, including type byte, four-byte PostgreSQL length field and body
allocation_impact: Inspect the five-byte backend header first and reject any total above 131207 (announced PostgreSQL length above 131206; body above 131202) before reserve, growth or a read target derived from the peer length. Larger admitted messages than the 8192-byte reusable scratch require separately owned same-root R/T backing reserved before allocation.
boundary_tests: 131207 total wire bytes accepted only when the message-specific structural/profile checks and existing root funding also pass
131208 total wire bytes, announced length 131207, or any checked arithmetic overflow rejected as UNAVAILABLE immediately after the five-byte header and before peer-length-driven allocation/growth
Prepared/binary row-bearing qualification proves the bound is never applied to a simple/text DataRow path
notes: First-slice PostgreSQL-specific cap. The selected prepared/binary DataRow maximum is 1 type + 4 length + 2 field count + (32 * 4 field-length prefixes) + 131072 admitted row-value bytes = 131207. This is not DFR-SQL-RESULT-BYTES and does not reuse FND02-WIRE-FRAME-BYTES.
